$comment: GENRES — the composition ring. A genre is a named complete look: it picks
one skin and one theme, adds ornament, and says which skeletons it suits.
AUTHORED, NEVER COMPUTED. Nothing generates entries in this file. The moment
a look falls out of a parameter combination it stops being a point of view,
which is the exact failure the skin ring was added to fix. If you find
yourself writing a loop over skins x themes, stop.
ONE SKIN, ONE THEME. A genre carries no alternatives. Two looks that differ
only in skin, where choosing between them is itself a stance, are SIBLINGS
in a FAMILY — two genres, not one with options. `family` below is a finding
aid exactly like `facets`; it groups genres and never composes one.
`why` is not documentation, it is the genre. A named look with no stated
point of view is a preset.

genres.name: Control Panel

facets.ideology: the operator knows what they are doing

why: This one was Gary's, and it arrived as a complaint. Looking at bevel on
the theme demos he said the mid grey was 'fuggly' on black or white —
then, immediately: 'It might be alright in cpanel.' Both halves are
right, and together they are the definition of a genre. A look is not
good or bad on its own; it is good FOR something. bevel's grey is dead
on a portfolio and correct on a machine you operate.
graphite because it is the one theme with no editorial opinion — the
others each carry a mood (blueprint's cyan, oxide's rust, vellum's
paper) that would compete with the chrome. bevel's face is derived from
the theme's ground, so a theme that is already neutral produces the
least surprising panel.
dark because the panel separates more from the page there — 2.46
against the page in dark, 1.92 in light, measured. In this genre that
separation is the point: the chrome should read as apparatus, not as
the document.
app-shell alone because a rail plus a dense table IS this genre's
argument. Portfolio and editorial would fight it; the storefront is a
shop, not an instrument.

genres.name: Control Surface

facets.ideology: the reading matters; the apparatus does not

why: The sibling to control-panel, and the first pair in a family. Same
theme, same skeleton, one skin apart — which is the exact shape the
family rule describes, and until there were two of them it was a word
in this file rather than something the suite could show.
The stance is not really about bevels. control-panel says every
control is equal and every one is named: uppercase mono labels at the
weight of the values, packed tight, because an operator who knows the
layout is hunting a specific cell and everything must be findable at
the same speed. This one says the READING is the thing — large quiet
numbers, labels demoted, more air — because the operator is watching a
handful of values change and the rest is context.
Choosing between those is itself a point of view, which is the test
that makes them two genres instead of one with a switch. Nobody would
shrug at getting the other one.
cushion because soft relief is the present tense of the same claim
bevel makes — that a surface has a lit edge and a shaded one. It also
leaves --ui-surface alone, which is why this genre needs no colour
exception where its sibling needed one for the caption bar.
graphite dark and app-shell are held FIXED from control-panel, not
chosen again. Varying more than one ring would make the pair a
comparison of two looks rather than a demonstration of what a skin is.
